title: Antimicrobial Allergy Assessment and Penicillin De-Labelling Referral
specialty: Allergy and Immunology / Infectious Diseases / Primary Care

evidenceAudit.scope: Structured assessment of a reported antimicrobial allergy and referral for specialist confirmation or de-labelling.
findings: Rebuilt against the approved-topic structure: a tiered investigation panel, time-ordered management and an explicit medicine decision pathway.
Every investigation row includes a reference or normal state, condition finding and next action.
Previous outline and published rows remain preserved; this additive version is pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: No topic-specific Saudi national guideline was found in the opened Saudi Ministry of Health protocol index unless a Saudi source is explicitly cited in the medicine row.
Current live Saudi Food and Drug Authority product registration was not individually confirmed; clinicians must check the hospital formulary.
Local antibiogram, resistance pattern, shared-care agreement and imaging availability require site-level confirmation where relevant.

pathophysiology.summary: Immediate immune-mediated reactions usually begin rapidly and may involve skin, airway or circulation. Delayed immune reactions range from benign exanthem to severe cutaneous or organ injury. Many recorded penicillin allergies reflect intolerance, coincidental illness or an unverified childhood event.
keyMechanisms: Immediate immune-mediated reactions usually begin rapidly and may involve skin, airway or circulation.
Delayed immune reactions range from benign exanthem to severe cutaneous or organ injury.
Many recorded penicillin allergies reflect intolerance, coincidental illness or an unverified childhood event.

references.title: NICE CG183: Drug allergy—diagnosis and management

symptoms: Record the culprit drug, indication, timing after each dose, number of doses, symptoms, treatment and outcome.
physicalSigns: Document rash morphology, mucosal involvement, angioedema, bronchospasm, hypotension and organ injury.
redFlags: Anaphylaxis, severe cutaneous adverse reaction, mucosal blistering, organ injury or haemolysis requires permanent high-visibility documentation and specialist advice.
precipitants: Re-exposure to the culprit or a cross-reacting antimicrobial.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Dose-related nausea, diarrhoea or headache without immune features.
Rash temporally linked to the illness and not reproducible with the medicine.
Airway, breathing or circulation compromise with compatible acute onset.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Refer after suspected anaphylaxis or severe non-immediate cutaneous reaction; consider referral when beta-lactams and at least one other antibiotic class cannot be used (CG183 section 1.4).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Timing and phenotype compatible with immediate or delayed allergy
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Record drug, route, indication, dose timing, number of doses, reaction, treatment and outcome.

ruleIn.testName: Clinical examination during an acute reaction
ruleIn.normalValue: No urticaria, mucosal lesion, bronchospasm or circulatory compromise
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Objective skin, airway, breathing, circulation or organ involvement
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Defines severity and whether the acute anaphylaxis or severe cutaneous reaction pathway is required.

ruleIn.testName: Acute mast-cell tryptase after suspected anaphylaxis
ruleIn.expectedFinding: A time-related rise can support mast-cell activation
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Take using the anaphylaxis sampling schedule; a normal result does not exclude anaphylaxis.
Provides the comparator for the acute sample and can identify a need for further specialist work-up.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Positive validated response to the suspected medicine
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Only an allergy service should select reagents and interpret the result.

ruleOut.expectedFinding: A positive response compatible with the phenotype
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Used selectively by specialists; not appropriate for every reaction.

ruleOut.normalValue: No objective reaction during the protocol
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Selected specialist confirmation test; do not use after severe delayed reactions.

clinicalManagement.title: Correct the allergy record
actions: Separate drug allergy from non-allergic adverse effects.
Record drug, reaction, severity, date, timing, route and drugs/classes to avoid.

clinicalManagement.title: Choose referral urgency
actions: Refer severe immediate or severe delayed reactions to specialist allergy services.
Do not perform an unsupervised oral challenge in primary care.

clinicalManagement.title: Close the loop after testing
actions: Update every active medication record and give the patient written information.
State the exact drugs now permitted and any drugs still contraindicated.

medicationPlan.note: Assessment, skin testing and drug provocation are specialist diagnostic procedures, not routine drug treatment. Treat an acute reaction through the separate anaphylaxis or severe cutaneous adverse-reaction pathway.

teaching.scope: Structured assessment of a reported antimicrobial allergy and referral for specialist confirmation or de-labelling.
learningObjectives: Recognise the condition and its red flags.
Choose initial tests without delaying urgent escalation.
Use a named multidisciplinary disposition plan.
keyPoints: Anaphylaxis, severe cutaneous adverse reaction, mucosal blistering, organ injury or haemolysis requires permanent high-visibility documentation and specialist advice.
Update every active medication record and give the patient written information.
pitfalls: Stopping after a short outline instead of documenting the full investigation pathway.
Using a medicine row without checking the branch, allergy, organ function, culture result and local formulary.
Mistaking publication status for clinical approval; this version remains pending until a clinician approves it.

patientEducation: Explain the working diagnosis, immediate plan and specific return or deterioration signs.
lifestyleAndDiet: Address prevention and self-management only after the acute safety plan is complete.
dischargeCriteria: Reaction phenotype and avoidance advice documented; urgent reactions treated; referral and patient information completed.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Reconcile the allergy field after the specialist report and at every transition of care.
